definition: Pattern search (also known as direct search, derivative-free search, or black-box search) is a family of numerical optimization methods that does not require a gradient.
details: As a result, it can be used on functions that are not continuous or differentiable. One such pattern search method is "convergence" (see below), which is based on the theory of positive bases. Optimization attempts to find the best match (the solution that has the lowest error value) in a multidimensional analysis space of possibilities.

explainer.lead: A family of numerical optimization methods that finds the best solution without using gradients. This lets it handle functions that are not continuous or differentiable, where gradient-based methods fail.

tiers.eli5: Instead of following a slope downhill, you try a set of nearby steps and keep the ones that make things better, repeating until you stop improving.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to tune black-box objectives such as simulator outputs or hardware settings where no derivative is available. A common pitfall is slow convergence, since many function evaluations may be needed.
tiers.paperLevel: Pattern search methods are derivative-free; one such method, convergence, is based on the theory of positive bases. Optimization searches a multidimensional space for the solution with the lowest error value.

explainer.example: Tuning three controller parameters by testing each point of a fixed step pattern around the current setting, moving to the best point, and repeating until no point improves the error.
